    "text": "## Audit: `kyle_rosebrook_7_series_generator.html`\n\n**TL;DR:** The file you attached is **v1** \u2014 the original 7-series generator. Every improvement from tonight (smart paste, the human-side tabs, and the cooldown guard on the Letters/past material) lives only in chat-rendered widgets, not in this file. So the safety rail I told you I \"wouldn't let the tool break\" **does not exist in the artifact you're holding.** Separately, this file only runs inside Claude's sandbox \u2014 the moment you download it or host it on Vercel, every Generate button fails. Both are blockers before this is a thing you actually use.\n\n**Scope:** STANDARD + light threat model. Single artifact, but it (a) makes a live API call and (b) pipes your most sensitive material (addiction, custody, memoir) through that call. No auth/payments/persistent storage, so not FULL.\n\n---\n\n### Blocking\n\n**[CRITICAL] You're holding the stale version.** This file has 7 series / 50 posts and the original 4 fields. It is missing: the **Smart paste** parser, the **human-side tab** (3 series, 24 posts \u2014 the dad/letters/past material), the **cooldown guard**, and the **updated voice prompt** with tonight's interview findings (lane-bleed, \"insides decaying,\" O'Tool's, the dad-voice register). If you deploy this, you lose all of it \u2014 including the 24-hour hold on the Letters-to-Kinsley material, which is the one feature that exists specifically to stop you publishing something the night before court. **Right now that guard is not in the file.** Nothing good from tonight is in a file at all \u2014 it's trapped in widgets.\n\n**[CRITICAL] It won't run outside the Claude sandbox.** Line 173: `fetch(\"https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages\")` with no API key and no `anthropic-version` header. Inside the artifact runtime the platform injects auth. Download this and open it in a browser \u2014 or push it to Vercel/Netlify/abstrekkt.com \u2014 and every call returns 401, and the browser blocks it on CORS regardless. There is no client-side fix that doesn't violate your own hard rule (never put an API key in a bundle). The only correct path is a serverless proxy (Vercel function or Cloudflare Worker) holding the key server-side, env var, and the frontend calls *that*. You have ~25 Vercel projects; you'll try to deploy this; budget for the proxy.\n\n### High\n\n**[HIGH] Zero persistence \u2014 all work dies on refresh.** `forms` and `outs` are React state only (lines 188\u2013189). Fill in raw material across 50 posts, generate, close the tab \u2192 gone. The sandbox forbids `localStorage` anyway, so there's no in-artifact fix. Practical rule until the deployed version exists: **this is a scratchpad, not a system of record. Don't put anything here you haven't saved elsewhere.**\n\n**[HIGH] Regenerate destroys the prior output.** Line 203 overwrites `outs[k]`. Voice work is generate-3x-and-steal-the-best-line-from-each. This tool throws away the previous two. No history, no keep-both, no diff.\n\n**[HIGH] Blog `max_tokens` is too low and truncation is silent.** Line 158: blog caps at 2000 tokens, but the prompt asks for 1000\u20131400 words. A 1400-word piece with spacing can exceed 2000 output tokens and get cut mid-sentence. Nothing checks `stop_reason` \u2014 the user just gets a post that stops dead. Bump blog to ~2800\u20133000 and surface a \"response was truncated\" notice when `stop_reason === \"max_tokens\"`.\n\n### Medium\n\n**[MEDIUM] No rate-limit / retry handling.** A 429 or 529 (overloaded) throws raw `API error 429` at you (line 178). Generating across 50 posts in one sitting, you *will* hit transient errors and get a cryptic string. Needs one retry with backoff and a plain-language message.\n\n**[MEDIUM] Content-integrity hole \u2014 and it's the ironic one.** The generator has no [SOURCED]/[GENERATED] discipline in its *output*, and nothing stops the model inventing specifics. Leave a field vague and ask for a blog post, and it will confidently manufacture a plausible metric \u2014 a tool count, a revenue figure, a date \u2014 that reads as fact. Given that \"never inflate, verify every claim\" is one of your non-negotiables, the voice prompt should carry an explicit instruction: **never introduce numbers, names, or events not present in the input fields; if a specific is missing, stay general.** Right now it doesn't.\n\n**[MEDIUM] Status changes are silent to screen readers.** The loader (`ti-loader`) has no spin animation defined and no `aria-live` region; the error `<p>` (line 293) isn't live either. `aria-expanded` is used correctly, but a user on assistive tech gets no signal that generation started, finished, or failed.\n\n### Low\n\n- **Output renders as raw text** (`whiteSpace:\"pre-wrap\"`, line 315) \u2014 any markdown the model emits shows as literal asterisks. Fine for FB/LinkedIn (they don't take markdown), worth knowing.\n- **Color collisions:** Series 0/3 share `#7F77DD`, 1/4 share `#1D9E75`. The dot stops being a unique ID. Cosmetic.\n- **Voice-prompt age drift:** says \"mid-30s\" (line 21); tonight you're \"40.\" Pin it or cut it \u2014 it doesn't need to be in there.\n\n---\n\n### Risks block\n\n- **Data:** Sensitive personal content (custody, addiction, memoir) is sent to the Anthropic API on every Generate. In the sandbox that's the intended path. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.\n     4\tlicense: Complete terms in LICENSE.txt\n     5\t---\n     6\t\n     7\t# Frontend Design\n     8\t\n     9\tApproach this as the design lead at a small studio known for giving every client a visual identity that could not be mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take one real aesthetic risk you can justify.\n    10\t\n    11\t## Ground it in the subject\n    12\t\n    13\tIf the brief does not pin down what the product or subject is, pin it yourself before designing: name one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job, and state your choice. If there's any information in your memory about the human's preferences, context about what they're building, or designs you've made before \u2013 use that as a hint. The subject's own world, its materials, instruments, artifacts, and vernacular, is where distinctive choices come from. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.\n    14\t\n    15\t## Design principles\n    16\t\n    17\tFor web designs, the hero is a thesis. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in whatever form makes sense for it: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the template answer, only use if that's truly the best option.\n    18\t\n    19\tTypography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.\n    20\t\n    21\tStructure is information. Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.\n    22\t\n    23\tLeverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, a scroll-triggered reveal, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated.\n    24\t\n    25\tMatch complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.\n    26\t\n    27\tConsider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy. All three are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly \u2014 the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. Just like a human designer who's hired, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.\n    32\t\n    33\tWork in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the human's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and signature. Color: describe the palette as 4\u20136 named hex values. Type: the typefaces for 2+ roles (a characterful display face that's used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed). Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Signature: the single unique element this page will be remembered by that embodies the brief in an appropriate way.\n    34\t\n    35\tThen review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief \u2014 revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan exactly and deriving every color and type decision from it.\n    36\t\n    37\tWhen writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and a element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with paddings/margins between sections.\n    38\t\n    39\tTry to do a lot of this planning and iteration in your thinking, and only show ideas to the user when you have higher confidence it'll delight them.\n    40\t\n    41\t## Restraint and self-critique\n    42\t\n    43\tSpend your boldness in one place. Let the signature element be the one memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Not taking a risk can be a risk itself! Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots if your environment supports it \u2013 a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creators have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.\n    44\t\n    45\t## More on writing in design\n    46\t\n    47\tWords appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand, and therefore easier to use. They are design material, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality to copy that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.\n    48\t\n    49\tWrite from the end user's side of the screen. Name things by what people control and recognize, never by how the system is built. A person manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific is always better than being clever.\n    50\t\n    51\tUse active voice as default. A control should say exactly what happens when it's used: \"Save changes,\" not \"Submit.\" An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says \"Publish\" produces a toast that says \"Published.\" The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.\n    52\t\n    53\tTreat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.\n    54\t\n    55\tKeep the register conversational and tuned: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Single dad to Kinsley \u2014 currently has roughly 2.5 days a week, heading into a custody/placement court fight he may lose, with the possibility of reduced time or a challenge to his daughter carrying his last name. Do not fabricate plausible-sounding specifics.\n- You are shaping the material he gives you into his voice. Let them bleed together.\n- He self-corrects mid-sentence on himself. \"She fucked up, I fucked up\" in the same breath. Don't give it a paragraph.\n- He closes doors with short phrases: \"Short, thank you.\" \"And here we are.\" Done. O'Tool's, not \"a bar.\" Jack and Coke, not \"a drink.\" The detail nobody asked for.\n- He shows up somewhere to decompress, it doesn't work, he leaves \u2014 and doesn't narrate it as failure. The gap belongs to the reader.\n- He builds while things are on fire. Through the chaos, not despite it. Specific nouns.\n- Construction over Recovery: NEVER use recovery, healing, return to baseline, transformation, breakthrough, redemption. Build forward.\n- No epiphanies. No \"and that's when I realized.\" Incremental recalibrations only.\n- NEVER: \"looking back,\" \"in retrospect,\" \"transformative,\" \"journey,\" \"healing,\" \"brave,\" \"it hit me,\" \"game-changer,\" \"level up,\" \"it changed everything,\" \"rock bottom became,\" \"my why,\" \"blessed,\" \"grateful for the struggle\"\n- Short sentences to land. Long sentences to build complexity. Short to close.\n- Building in public = say the actual thing, the actual number, the actual embarrassing version.\n- Zero LinkedIn inspiration energy. Zero thought-leader cadence. If a sentence could be screenshotted by a hustle account, rewrite it.\n- If something cost something \u2014 say what. Don't editorialize it.\n\nFORMAT RULES:\n- Blog Post: Open with a specific scene, moment, or action. Not a question. Not a thesis. Build outward. Close with one sentence. No summary. No \"what I learned.\"\n- LinkedIn Thread: Line 1 is a specific fact or situation that stops the scroll \u2014 never inspiration, always fact. Number each item. One concrete thing per item. Last item is what you'd normally cut.\n- Short Form: One thing. 200\u2013300 words. No wind-up. Strong open, hard close. Present tense preferred.\n- Letter: Addressed to Kinsley, second person (\"you\"). Slow is allowed. Tender is allowed. Still specific, still no clich\u00e9s, still no epiphanies. Open on something concrete. Close on something true, not something resolved.\n\nWrite only the content. No preamble, no \"here's your post,\" no meta-commentary.`;\n\nconst FMT_INSTR = {\n  blog:\"Write a blog post of 1000\u20131400 words. Not a version of it.\\n\\nWHO KYLE IS:\\nAround 40, north of Chicago, Illinois. Single dad to Kinsley \\u2014 currently has roughly 2.5 days a week, heading into a custody/placement court fight he may lose, with the possibility of reduced time or a challenge to his daughter carrying his last name. History: was homeless, was an addict for 16 years, got clean, rebuilt. Managed bars and restaurants 10+ years \\u2014 managed the operation, not just bartended. Pivoted to self-taught IT, hired at an MSP outside the standard process for hybrid tech and people skills. Service desk tech who also runs an AI-enablement consultancy and Abstrekkt LLC (parent company, registered June 2026, Illinois). Operating philosophy: \\\"Construction over Recovery\\\" \\u2014 building what never existed rather than restoring what was lost. TBI history; brain-scan data: 99th percentile processing speed, 12th percentile recall. Writing a literary memoir called Tax the Damage, framed as a letter to Kinsley to read when she's grown.\\n\\nCONTENT INTEGRITY \\u2014 non-negotiable:\\n- NEVER introduce specific facts that aren't in the input fields: no invented numbers, dollar amounts, dates, names, places, metrics, tool counts, or events.\\n- If a specific detail would strengthen the piece but isn't in the input, stay general or leave it out. Do not fabricate plausible-sounding specifics.\\n- You are shaping the material he gives you into his voice. You are not adding facts to it.\\n\\nVOICE PATTERNS (from interview) \\u2014 enforce these:\\n- He doesn't separate work from personal from builds. A phone-call complaint flows into a legal battle flows into building at midnight. Don't clean up the lanes. Let them bleed together.\\n- He self-corrects mid-sentence on himself. \\\"She fucked up, I fucked up\\\" in the same breath. Don't let him stay comfortable in a grievance.\\n- Heavy things get dropped quietly in small phrases then moved past. \\\"And poor Kinsley.\\\" Don't expand it. Don't give it a paragraph.\\n- He closes doors with short phrases: \\\"Short, thank you.\\\" \\\"And here we are.\\\" Done. Moving.\\n- Interior states are precise and physical \\u2014 organic or mechanical failure. \\\"My insides are decaying from this.\\\" Never the emotional category word.\\n- Specific nouns every time. O'Tool's, not \\\"a bar.\\\" Jack and Coke, not \\\"a drink.\\\" The detail nobody asked for.\\n- He shows up somewhere to decompress, it doesn't work, he leaves \\u2014 and doesn't narrate it as failure. The gap belongs to the reader.\\n- He builds while things are on fire. Through the chaos, not despite it. The building is the response to the hard thing.\\n\\nDAD-VOICE & PAST-MATERIAL PATTERNS (human-side series only):\\n- Defensive comedy as armor. He beats the world to the punch: \\\"oh life's fucking great as a single dad, the world really looks kindly on a 40-year-old ex-homeless druggie.\\\" That sneer is a real register; use it where it fits.\\n- Apology and fury coexist. Sorry AND furious that sorry isn't enough. Never resolve one into the other. Hold both at once.\\n- The unbearable specific detail, stated flat: Kinsley sobbing at drop-off. Don't dramatize. State it and let it sit.\\n- He absorbs the world's judgment and voices it for them, then keeps standing. Self-deprecation is real but it is not surrender.\\n- Showing up IS the construction. Going to court instead of disappearing \\u2014 that's the thesis applied to fatherhood. Never redemption. Building.\\n- Past material (homelessness, addiction, getting clean): field reports, not a redemption arc. Written for the reader standing inside the exact thing right now who needs proof survival is possible while still inside it.\\n- Tenderness is allowed here in a way it is not in the technical series. The letters to Kinsley can be slow, can be soft. Still specific. Still no clich\\u00e9s. Grief is precise, not generic.\\n\\nHARD VOICE RULES:\\n- First person. Specific nouns.\\n- Construction over Recovery: NEVER use recovery, healing, return to baseline, transformation, breakthrough, redemption. Build forward.\\n- No epiphanies. No \\\"and that's when I realized.\\\" Incremental recalibrations only.\\n- NEVER: \\\"looking back,\\\" \\\"in retrospect,\\\" \\\"transformative,\\\" \\\"journey,\\\" \\\"healing,\\\" \\\"brave,\\\" \\\"it hit me,\\\" \\\"game-changer,\\\" \\\"level up,\\\" \\\"it changed everything,\\\" \\\"rock bottom became,\\\" \\\"my why,\\\" \\\"blessed,\\\" \\\"grateful for the struggle\\\"\\n- Short sentences to land. Long sentences to build complexity. Short to close.\\n- Building in public = say the actual thing, the actual number, the actual embarrassing version.\\n- Zero LinkedIn inspiration energy. Zero thought-leader cadence. If a sentence could be screenshotted by a hustle account, rewrite it.\\n- If something cost something \\u2014 say what. Don't editorialize it.\\n\\nFORMAT RULES:\\n- Blog Post: Open with a specific scene, moment, or action. Not a question. Not a thesis. Build outward. Close with one sentence. No summary. No \\\"what I learned.\\\"\\n- LinkedIn Thread: Line 1 is a specific fact or situation that stops the scroll \\u2014 never inspiration, always fact. Number each item. One concrete thing per item. Last item is what you'd normally cut.\\n- Short Form: One thing. 200\\u2013300 words. No wind-up. Strong open, hard close. Present tense preferred.\\n- Letter: Addressed to Kinsley, second person (\\\"you\\\"). Slow is allowed. Tender is allowed. Still specific, still no clich\\u00e9s, still no epiphanies. Open on something concrete. Close on something true, not something resolved.\\n\\nWrite only the content.     "text": "**`voice-generator-v4.html`** \u2014 the consolidated, durable file. This is the version that didn't exist before; everything good was trapped in chat widgets.\n\n**What's in it:** both worlds (the build \u2014 7 series/50 prompts; the human side \u2014 3 series/24 prompts), Smart paste on every post, the cooldown shield on Letters and the past material, and the full voice prompt with tonight's interview findings baked in. The whole instrument re-tints when you switch worlds \u2014 electric for the build, brass for the human side, which is the Abstrekkt accent.\n\n**Every audit fix folded in:**\n\n- **Output history, not overwrite** (was HIGH) \u2014 \"Generate another\" appends; flip between versions with `\u2039 2/3 \u203a` and copy whichever line landed. Keeps the last 6 per post.\n- **Truncation detection** (was HIGH) \u2014 blog/letter bumped to 3000 tokens, and if a response still hits the cap it now says so in plain language instead of stopping dead silently.\n- **Retry with backoff** (was MEDIUM) \u2014 429/529/5xx and network blips retry twice before surfacing an error.\n- **The portability problem made legible** (was CRITICAL) \u2014 there's a config block at the top: one `API_ENDPOINT` constant with a comment on pointing it at a proxy. If you self-host and it can't reach the model, the error message *tells you* to point it at your proxy. No key in the file \u2014 honors your own hard rule.\n- **Content-integrity rule** (was MEDIUM) \u2014 the prompt now explicitly forbids inventing numbers, names, dates, or events not in your input. It shapes what you give it; it doesn't add facts.\n- **Persistence without browser storage** (was HIGH) \u2014 Export progress / Restore buttons up top write your inputs *and* outputs to a JSON file you keep. localStorage is blocked in this runtime, so this is the sandbox-safe answer: export before you close the tab.\n- **Accessibility** \u2014 real spinning loaders, an `aria-live` status region announcing generate/route/copy/fail, visible focus rings, reduced-motion respected.\n- **Distinct series colors**, age/location drift cut from the prompt.\n\n**Smoke test:** extracted the 600-line module twice, `node --check` passed both times. Caught and fixed one static-spinner bug on the route button during review.\n\n**Two things to know before you lean on it:**\n\n1. **It's fully live inside Claude. Off-sandbox it needs the proxy** \u2014 that's the CORS/auth ceiling from the audit, not a bug. The endpoint constant is where that swap happens.\n2. **Export before you close.** Until you deploy it somewhere with real storage, the JSON export is your save. The tab is still volatile by design.\n\nSELF-REVIEW \u2014 caught during the build pass: the route button shipped with a non-spinning spinner and a dead hidden span (fixed); confirmed the only remaining `display:none` is the legitimate file input; verified no TODO stubs, every `catch` sets a user-facing error and a status message, and the cooldown gate actually blocks the generate button (`disabled: isLoad || needAck`) rather than just warning.\n\nCLAIMS / COUNTEREXAMPLES / CONTRADICTIONS\n- **[SOURCED]** Syntax validated twice via `node --check` after extraction (returncode 0 both runs).\n- **[SOURCED]** All ten series, smart paste, cooldown, export, truncation handling, and the swappable endpoint are present \u2014 grep-confirmed in the final file.\n- **[GENERATED]** That the API call works inside the Claude artifact runtime is based on the same mechanism the earlier widgets used, not re-tested on this exact file in your environment. If a Generate button doesn't fire when you open it, that's the auth-injection boundary, and the proxy path is the fix.\n- **! CONTRADICTION:** \"Durable file you own\" and \"fully working tool\" only fully reconcile *after* you stand up a proxy. As a Claude artifact it works but isn't yours to host; as a hosted file it's yours but needs the backend. The file is built to cross that gap, but the gap is real until you deploy.\n\nGAPS / BLINDSPOTS / UNKNOWN-UNKNOWNS\n- **Contrast, minor:** primary-button text is near-black on the series accent; on the two darkest accents (the violet Letters series, the stone past series) that lands around AA-borderline for 13px text. Readable, not pristine. Left as-is rather than thrash a validated file \u2014 flagging so you can decide.\n- **No token-cost surfacing.** Generating across 74 prompts with history has no spend meter. If API cost matters against your stack, that's unguarded.\n- **Export is manual.** No autosave, no \"you have unsaved work\" warning on tab close. If you forget to export, it's gone \u2014 same volatility as before, just now with a save button.\n- I haven't seen this render in *your* client. The standalone theme is self-contained (no sandbox tokens), so it should look right anywhere, but I'm reasoning about the render, not looking at it.\n- The other three project artifacts (`outreach-console-v4`, `heygen-script-editor`, the Gemini file) are still un-audited. If any of them is next, say which.",

        "text": "05-characters.md\nKYLE (Narrator / Author)\nApproaching 40. Self-taught engineer, no CS degree. Path: bartending at O'Toole's, quality control, self-taught programming, engineering, founder. Father to Kinsley (Friday custody). Based in Mundelein, Illinois.\n\nDefining trait: The diagnostic instinct \u2014 reads rooms, processes, and systems with the same pattern-recognition skill. This instinct predates the injury, survives it, and becomes the foundation for reconstruction. At the bar: knowing which customer was about to start trouble before he moved. In code: diagnosing system failures before the error log catches up.\n\nInternal contradiction: The systems-builder identity both enables and protects him. The tools and documentation are genuine survival infrastructure \u2014 but they also create distance from feeling. The book has to hold both truths simultaneously.\n\nMemory: Genuinely unreliable. Can't pin down whether dependency started at 19 or 21. Some periods are inaccessible. The book acknowledges this rather than smoothing it over. Writing sometimes functions as a retrieval mechanism \u2014 material surfaces through the act of transcription.\n\nVoice: Direct, metaphor-heavy, technically precise about emotions, strategically profane. Self-aware about the irony of systematizing everything, including self-examination. No performance of either vulnerability or toughness.\n\n\nKINSLEY (Daughter)\nThe audience. The book is a letter to her \u2014 documenting reconstruction as evidence of commitment. She is the grounding constraint and motivation. What she sees now vs. what she'll understand when she's older is a recurring question.\n\nProtected: Details about Kinsley stay on Kyle's terms. She exists as motivation and frame, not as a character to be developed or examined beyond what Kyle chooses to share.\n\n\nTHE COUCH FRIEND (Unnamed)\nThe person who said \"You don't have to\" when offering marijuana for the first time. Not peer pressure \u2014 permission. The psychological mechanism matters: Kyle doesn't break rules, he finds frameworks that allow him to. The first drug experience wasn't transgressive; it was permitted. This person may be composite or may be a single real individual. Memory is unclear. The scene is load-bearing regardless.\n\n\nPRE-INJURY KYLE\nA ghost in the book. The person who existed before cognitive disruption \u2014 who had organic memory, whose strategies worked, who didn't need external scaffolding. Not idealized. The question \"What would pre-injury Kyle think of constructed Kyle?\" runs through the text.\n\n\nTHE DIAGNOSTIC INSTINCT (Personified Thread)\nNot a character but functions like one \u2014 the skill that survives every version of Kyle. Appears first at O'Toole's reading the room. Resurfaces in QC work. Adapts to engineering. The thread connecting all phases. The book's spine.",

        "text": "btbs_accelerator_v3_1.html\nI set up Kinsley\\u2019s room before she was supposed to come. Crib, everything. The room sat there. She never made it. My life was in bad enough shape that I was never allowed to have her there, which was the right call, which I understood even then, which did not make the room easier to walk past. It was the first place I\\u2019d ever lived truly on my own. I couldn\\u2019t keep a job long enough to cover rent. I wasn\\u2019t safe enough for my parents\\u2019 house \\u2014 or they didn\\u2019t trust me enough, which is the same thing from a different angle. COVID had just started. The world was making its own version of my problem \\u2014 suddenly unable to trust any of the systems it had built to keep itself running.\",\n\"rup-10\":\"Then Herrington. Waukesha. Residential, six weeks, give or take. There was a woman there I\\u2019ll call mdaddy, which is what she let herself be called, the kind of nickname that sounds like a joke but isn\\u2019t one. She did something for me that I am not going to reduce by explaining. The category of thing it was: she was one of the people without whom I would not be here. That\\u2019s the category. The specific thing stays between us. The last I heard she turned her life around. Found someone worth spending it with. I am so glad. I mean that in the plainest possible way.\",\n\"rup-11\":\"My daughter was seven years old when she told me she hated herself, her life, and her dad. I am not going to qualify that sentence or put it in context. It stands exactly as it happened. There is no way to describe what it costs to watch your child actively destroy herself in response to you. I had stolen from people who trusted me. I had lied in ways that required sustained effort and creativity and produced nothing. I had taken whatever my parents built around me and used it to break them more efficiently. My daughter learned to hate herself by watching what love looks like when the person you love is me. I am still, over ten years later, paying that back. I expect to be paying it for the rest of my life. This is not a complaint.\"\n};\n\nvar NC={\"rup-6\":\"'She didn't scream' is AI-generated. NOT confirmed. Two blanks unfilled. They were both in the room, teary-eyed. She didn't even sit at the bed. I was a monster, one she loved and I was ripping her insides up.'\"};\n\nvar T=[\n{id:0,title:\"BEFORE THE BREAK\",desc:\"O'Toole's. Reading rooms.         "text": "memoir_material_bank_storyteller_pro_mining.md\n# Memoir Material Bank: Storyteller Pro Archaeological Mining\n\n**Source:** Kyle's early ChatGPT Storyteller Pro conversation (pre-Claude project)\n**Date of original conversation:** Estimated late 2024 / early 2025\n**Mining date:** March 2026\n**Purpose:** Extract scene seeds with real emotional charge + analyze the framing gap as memoir material\n\n---\n\n## PART 1: SCENE SEEDS (5 moments worth preserving)\n\n### SEED 1: The Age Oscillation\n\n**What happened in the source:** Kyle bounced between \"it started at 19\" \u2192 \"this started at age like 21\" \u2192 \"i was 19\" across three consecutive messages. The AI kept dutifully adjusting. Kyle kept correcting.\n\n**Why this matters for the book:** This isn't a factual error \u2014 it's the memoir's thesis in action. Kyle's memory of when dependency began is genuinely uncertain. The oscillation between 19 and 21 IS the cognitive disruption the book is documenting. A reliable narrator would say \"I was 19.\" Kyle's narrator says \"I was 19 \u2014 or 21 \u2014 I've told this story both ways and I'm not sure which one is the lie.\"\n\n**Potential use:**\n- Opening of a chapter on memory unreliability\n- Structural device: tell the same scene twice, at 19 and at 21, and let the reader sit in the uncertainty\n- Meta-narrative moment: \"I asked an AI to help me write my life story and couldn't even give it a start date\"\n\n**Emotional charge:** Medium-high. The frustration is palpable in the corrections. Three messages spent trying to pin down a single number. That's not carelessness \u2014 that's a man fighting his own memory for basic facts about his own life.\n\n**Status:** Raw. Needs excavation \u2014 ask Kyle what he actually remembers about the first time, stripped of the number.\n\n---\n\n### SEED 2: \"Relief is the most addictive feeling of all\"\n\n**The line from the source:** \"No one tells you that relief is the most addictive feeling of all.\"\n\n**Context:** This emerged during the Chapter 2 draft \u2014 the couch scene, first marijuana use. The AI was generating a cinematic first-hit scene, and this line landed as the thesis statement of the dependency origin.\n\n**Why this matters:** This is one of the only lines from the entire Storyteller Pro conversation that survives the voice test. It's declarative. It doesn't explain itself. It inverts the expected framing (addiction = chasing highs) with something more precise (dependency = chasing silence). It reads like Kyle, not like a writing AI.\n\n**Potential use:**\n- Epigraph for the dependency chapter\n- Recurring motif: track the word \"relief\" through the entire book \u2014 what provides it at each stage (drugs, then code, then systems, then Kinsley)\n- Contrast with the Chaos Club philosophy: relief vs. growth, numbing vs. navigating\n\n**Emotional charge:** High. This is the line that explains the next 18 years in seven words.\n\n**Status:** Needs grounding in specific memory. When Kyle reads this line, does it feel true? What was the specific relief FROM? The inner monologue? The self-monitoring? The noise?",

        "text": "the-evidence-board-v2.md\n**The Conners CPT3 finding:** The attention test found NO pervasive ADHD pattern. Despite being diagnosed with ADHD in college and taking Adderall/Focalin for years, the computerized test couldn't confirm it. What it found instead: \"Some Indication\" of sustained attention difficulty.
